title: Long META — 12GW AMD Helios Anchor + Q2 FY2026 Earnings Eve
entry: $670–690 (intraday July 23). META reports Q2 FY2026 earnings AH Wednesday July 30. Today's AMD Lisa Su keynote confirmed META as the anchor of the 12GW Helios commitment (OpenAI + Meta = 12GW at $5–5.5M/rack), validating that META's AI infrastructure capex is translating into tangible GPU compute procurement rather than speculative capacity reservation. Enter at or below $685 to preserve full stop distance. Do not initiate above $695 — at that level the AMD-announcement premium has fully repriced today's catalyst.
stop_loss: $648 daily close (~4.6% below $679 reference) — at $648, the stock has broken below the July 21 pre-AMD-announcement base, implying that (1) Q2 guidance commentary or early Reels/advertising weakness is leaking into the pre-earnings channel checks; (2) GOOGL's $195–205B capex raise has re-activated the AI capex overhang narrative and is pulling META's valuation multiple lower alongside the sector; or (3) macro deterioration (VIX above 22, September hike confirmed) is compressing high-multiple growth stocks broadly. Below $648, the pre-earnings setup is broken.
targets: $715 — Q2 FY2026 EPS above consensus; Reels advertising revenue beats on CPM expansion; META confirms AI-driven ad targeting improvements lifting click-through rates 15–20%; +5.3% from $679 reference; cover 40% on post-earnings gap-up day

$748 — Meta AI monthly active user count disclosed at 1B+; advertising revenue guidance for Q3 above Street estimate; AI capex guidance for H2 explicitly cites Helios rack deployment timeline (H2 CY2026); Reality Labs operating loss narrows on Quest 4 pre-order momentum; +10.2%; cover 40% of remaining

$790 — Blue-sky: META announces a separate AI compute monetization layer (enterprise licensing of Meta AI infrastructure or Llama API); Q3 guidance implies 20%+ EPS growth; multiple expansion to 25x FY2027 EPS as the market re-rates META from pure social-advertising platform to AI infrastructure platform; +16.3%; hold final 20%
risk_reward: 1:3.6 to Target 3 from $679 reference (risk $31; T3 reward $111)
catalyst: Two simultaneous catalysts on July 23: (1) AMD Lisa Su keynote confirmed META as an anchor of the 12GW AMD Helios customer consortium ($5–5.5M/rack), directly validating the AI infrastructure investment thesis embedded in META's $60–65B FY2026 capex guidance; (2) META reports Q2 FY2026 earnings AH July 30, one week out. The earnings setup is constructive: GOOGL's Q2 Cloud +82% (reported July 22 AH) confirms that enterprise AI workload demand is real and scaling — the same advertising intelligence tailwinds that drove GOOGL's ad revenue are feeding META's Reels engagement metrics. Q2 consensus for META is approximately $5.85 EPS on $43B revenue.
thesis:
META's bull case has two distinct legs that are both catalyzed simultaneously on July 23. The first is the near-term earnings catalyst: META reports Q2 FY2026 AH on July 30, and the setup after GOOGL's Q2 beat is constructive. GOOGL's ad revenue exceeded expectations despite concerns about AI search cannibalization — the outcome that was most feared by META bulls (that AI search would erode advertiser ROI and CPM rates) did not materialize. If anything, GOOGL's strong ad result validates the premise that AI-enhanced targeting and engagement is growing the total digital advertising pie rather than redistributing it. META's Reels platform and AI-driven ad ranking systems are the most aggressive AI implementation in the advertising stack; the same tailwind applies.

The second leg is the structural AI infrastructure validation. The AMD 12GW Helios confirmation reveals that META is not merely spending $60–65B in FY2026 capex on growth-stage speculation — it is converting that commitment into specific rack purchases at $5M per rack alongside OpenAI. This matters for the valuation multiple: the bear case on META's capex has been that management is over-investing in AI infrastructure that won't yield returns for 3–5 years. The Helios commitment implies META is acquiring compute at a specific price, timeline, and scale — which is quantifiable. At $5.5M/rack and assuming META's share of the 12GW commitment is 50–60% of the compute ordered, META is deploying approximately $15–20B in Helios racks across 2026–2027. That compute is the physical infrastructure underpinning Meta AI (1B+ MAU target), which management has telegraphed as a direct advertising revenue multiplier through improved targeting precision.

At $679, META trades at approximately 22x consensus FY2026 EPS of $31 and 18x FY2027 EPS of $37. These are peer-average multiples for a company growing EPS at 20%+ with a dominant social media moat and an AI compute infrastructure build that is now verified rather than speculative. The PEG ratio on the 2-year forward growth trajectory is approximately 0.9x — below 1.0x implies the stock is undervalued on growth-adjusted terms. The Q2 earnings event one week out creates a defined catalyst for multiple re-rating.

The counter-party argues: (1) META's $60–65B capex trajectory is margin-dilutive and will suppress FCF through FY2027; (2) Reality Labs continues burning $4–5B quarterly with no clear path to profitability; (3) GOOGL's simultaneous capex expansion ($195–205B guidance raised) signals that the entire mega-cap tech group is in a capex arms race that will eventually compress returns. The bull response: Reality Labs losses are a known embedded cost; META FCF excluding Reality Labs was $15B+ in Q1; and the capex arms race is a winner-take-most dynamic where META's 3B daily active user base gives it the data advantage that converts infrastructure into monetizable AI products faster than any competitor.
bull_case: META Q2 EPS beats consensus ($5.85) at $6.20+; Q3 guidance above $44B revenue; Meta AI disclosed at 1.2B MAU; Reels CPM expansion confirmed for Q3; AMD Helios Helios commitment is formally disclosed in 10-Q capex schedule. Stock gaps to $720 AH July 30, continues to $748 by August 5 on buy-side upgrade cycle. T2 cover by August 8.
bear_case: GOOGL's $195–205B capex raise is read as sector-wide overinvestment signal that overrides individual fundamental beats; META misses Q2 EPS on Reality Labs opex spike or higher-than-expected Helios rack pre-payment charge; stock retreats to $645–$650 pre-stop zone. The $648 stop limits loss to ~$31/share (4.6%) on the reference price.
invalidation: $648 daily close (thesis structurally reset); OR META Q2 EPS below $5.50 (>6% miss vs consensus) on advertising weakness; OR management provides Q3 guidance below $41B revenue implying advertising slowdown rather than acceleration; OR AMD Helios 12GW commitment disclosed as non-binding or spread across 3+ years (reducing immediacy of compute ramp); OR macro regime deterioration pushes VIX above 22 and September hike probability to 85%+ before July 30 earnings
